sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The HASH_JOIN (node 8) processes 99K filtered trips rows with a CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) join condition, and the subsequent HASH_GROUP_BY aggregates these rows by string columns (Borough, Zone), causing high CPU for type conversion and string hashing.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

The CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) in the join condition forces a per-row type conversion on the 99K trips rows, adding CPU overhead; if PULocationID and LocationID shared the same integer type, the cast could be eliminated and the hash join would be faster.

The HASH_GROUP_BY (node 4) groups 99K rows by two string columns (Borough, Zone) which are not compressed in the join output, causing expensive string hashing and comparison; pre-aggregating trips by PULocationID before joining would reduce the input to at most 243 rows.

The RIGHT HASH_JOIN builds its hash table on the larger trips input (99K rows) rather than the smaller zones table (265 rows) because the preserved side is zones; reversing the join order (e.g., by rewriting as a LEFT JOIN with zones first) might allow building the hash table on zones.
